Project
Overview
ExpenseFlow
is
a
full-stack
personal
finance
application
designed
to
make
tracking
income,
expenses,
and
spending
habits
simple
and
intuitive.
The
project
is
a
browser-based
experience
with
secure
authentication,
transaction
management,
categories,
financial
summaries,
filtering,
and
visual
analytics.
The
application
uses
a
FastAPI
backend
with
PostgreSQL
persistence
and
a
dependency-free
HTML/CSS/JavaScript
frontend.

Purpose
and
Goals
The
project
is
centered
on
helping
users
track,
understand,
and
improve
their
personal
finances
without
adding
unnecessary
complexity.
The
frontend
is
intentionally
lightweight
and
dependency-free,
while
the
backend
centralizes
business
rules
such
as
transaction
ownership
and
category/type
validation.
User
authentication:
Register,
sign
in,
load
the
authenticated
profile,
handle
expired
sessions,
and
sign
out.
Financial
dashboard:
Display
balance,
total
income,
total
expenses,
monthly
spending,
category
spending,
and
recent
transactions.
Transaction
management:
Create,
list,
filter,
update,
retrieve,
and
delete
transactions.
Categories:
Load
categories
ordered
by
transaction
type
and
category
name.
Analytics:
Generate
expense
totals
by
category
and
by
month.
Responsive
experience:
Provide
desktop/mobile
UI
behavior
and
responsive
navigation.
Architecture
The
solution
follows
a
conventional
full-stack
web
architecture.
The
browser
loads
the
frontend
from
the
deployed
Vercel
site.
The
JavaScript
client
communicates
with
the
FastAPI
REST
API
over
HTTP.
The
backend
validates
inputs,
authenticates
requests,
applies
business
rules,
and
persists
data
in
PostgreSQL
through
SQLAlchemy.
Alembic
manages
database
schema
changes.
Application
Workflow
A
typical
user
journey
begins
by
creating
an
account
or
signing
in.
After
authentication,
the
frontend
retrieves
the
current
user,
financial
summary,
categories,
transactions,
category
totals,
and
monthly
totals.
Users
can
then
add,
filter,
inspect,
update,
or
delete
transactions
while
the
backend
continues
to
enforce
authentication
and
ownership.
Step
Action
System
behavior
1
Register
POST
/auth/register
creates
a
user
with
a
hashed
password.
2
Login
POST
/auth/login
verifies
the
password
and
returns
a
bearer
token.
3
Load
session
GET
/auth/me
resolves
the
authenticated
user
from
the
token.
4
Load
dashboard
The
frontend
requests
summary,
categories,
transactions
and
analytics
endpoints.
5

POST
/transactions/

before

/

/transactions/
supports

GET
/transactions/{id}

modifies

fields
while
re-
checking
category/type
consistency.
8

DELETE
/transactions/{id}
removes
an
owned
transaction.
Database
Layer
The
data
model
contains
three
primary
entities:
User,
Transaction,
and
Category.
Transaction
links
each
record
to
a
user
and
a
category.
Monetary
values
use
Numeric(10,
2),
and
category
names
are
unique
within
a
transaction
type.

Authentication
and
Security
Authentication
is
implemented
with
bearer
JWT
tokens.
During
registration,
the
password
is
hashed
before
being
stored.
During
login,
the
submitted
password
is
verified
against
the
stored
hash,
then
a
JWT
is
issued.
The
token
contains
the
user
ID
in
the
sub
claim
and
expires
after
30
minutes
in
the
current
backend
implementation.

OpenAPI/Swagger
UI
token
authentication
setup.

FastAPI
documentation
testing
the
user
login
endpoint
response.
REST
API
and
CRUD
Operations
The
FastAPI
backend
groups
endpoints
by
concern:
/auth
for
authentication,
/categories
for
categories,
/transactions
for
transaction
operations,
and
/summary
for
analytics.
Endpoint
Method
Purpose
/auth/register
POST
Create
a
new
user
account.
/auth/login
POST
Validate
credentials
and
issue
a
bearer
token.
/auth/me
GET
Return
the
current
authenticated
user
profile.
/categories/
GET
Return
available
categories
ordered
by
type
and
name.
/transactions/
GET
List
the
current
user’s
transactions;
optional
type/category_id
filters.
/transactions/{transaction_id}
GET
Retrieve
one
transaction
owned
by
the
current
user.
/transactions/
POST
Create
a
transaction
after
category/type
validation.
/transactions/{transaction_id}
PUT
Update
an
owned
transaction.
/transactions/{transaction_id}
DELETE
Delete
an
owned
transaction.
/summary/
GET
Return
total
income,
total
expenses,
and
balance.
/summary/categories
GET
Return
expense
totals
grouped
by
category.
/summary/monthly
GET
Return
expense
totals
grouped
by
year
and
month.

Frontend
The
frontend
is
dependency-free
and
implemented
with
HTML,
CSS,
and
JavaScript.
The
main
page
is
rendered
dynamically
into
the
app
element.
Local
storage
keeps
the
access
token
and
cached
user
profile;
API
calls
attach
the
bearer
token
when
present.

Deployment
The
frontend
is
deployed
on
Vercel
,
while
the
FastAPI
backend
is
deployed
separately
and
connects
to
the
PostgreSQL
database
.
This
setup
allows
the
application
to
serve
the
frontend
reliably
while
keeping
the
API
and
database
services
independent.
